name: Goyal Salt Limited
identity_note: Not Goyal Aluminiums, Goel Food Products or promoter-group salt units.
summary: Goyal Salt is an operating salt-refining and trading expansion story, not yet an evidence-backed compounder. Gujarat commissioning has produced real sales and operating-profit growth: FY26 standalone revenue reached ₹199.60 crore, up 53.58%, and manufactured sales rose to ₹118.17 crore. sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Exact security: Goyal Salt Limited, NSE SME GOYALSALT, ISIN INE0QFE01017. Information cutoff: 20 October 2026, India Standard Time; sources retrieved 21 October but only pre-cutoff information is used. Reference is the official NSE final close on 19 October, ₹100.75, not a live offer. Current issued equity is 17, 900, 250 shares; the eligible SM instrument is 19356 and lot size is 600. An illustrative ₹5 lakh position rounds down to eight lots, 4, 800 shares costing ₹483, 600. Nine lots cost ₹544, 050. This is a liquidity reference, not a recommended allocation.

Scope is audited standalone through March 2026 under the Companies (Accounting Standards) non-Ind-AS framework. The official integrated filing is explicitly non-Ind-AS and statutory policies use AS; generic MD&A wording says Ind AS and is retained as a disclosure inconsistency, not the adopted analytical basis. No subsidiary was controlled at that balance-sheet date according to Note 12. Exim and 51%-controlled Foods create a subsequent group perimeter whose current statements are unavailable. Do not splice a CRA analytical consolidation into these audited numbers. Forecast investor dates are 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031; nominal INR equity hurdle is 15%, before personal tax, with 12%/18% sensitivity. WACC is separately tested at 12%–16%.

G1 is Conditional, not Fail. G2 is Hold — unresolved for material cash-classification/restatement questions. G3 is Hold — unresolved for current funding and subsidiary uses. G4 is Hold — unresolved for incomplete trading-day observations and live implementation evidence. Confidence is High on identity, the official dated quote and disclosed current financial totals; Medium on underlying growth and normalized operating results; Low on attributable capital returns, current group funding and executable liquidity. Overall investment confidence is Low because the weakest material inputs control the conclusion. [S4–S10][M1][M2]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The thirteen factor audits are embedded, each with at least two material facts, contrary evidence and source IDs. Canonical factors are GOV5, MOAT4, REV7, DUR6, CAP NS, CASH3, BAL NS, EXEC6, EARN6; IAS factors R NS, D3, P4, L NS. BQS known contribution is exactly 4.02 at 80% coverage, with mathematical missing-data bounds 4.22–6.02. GQS known contribution is 5.20 at 85% coverage, with raw bounds 5.35–6.70. Persistent weak cash realization, not merely high capex, triggers the explicit GQS cap 5. The capped bound is 5.00–5.00 but the point remains NS because CAP is unverified; a capped interval does not license ranking an incomplete company at 5.

IAS reuses final BQS once at 25% and has 30% directly scoreable coverage: D contributes 0.60 and P0.40. Its direct missing-input bound is 1.70–8.00; propagating the tighter BQS bounds yields 2.505–7.005. These are exact Decimal bounds, not probabilities or confidence intervals. There is no undisclosed overall score and no renormalized weighting. No governance or funding-failure numerical override is applied because neither a severe governance failure nor actual unfinanceable default has been evidenced. G2 nevertheless precludes a favorable investment classification. Moving MOAT and EXEC by one point together shifts BQS bounds by 0.28; it cannot resolve missing CAP/BAL. The full score audit records each original weight and contribution. [S1–S10][M1][M2]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Goyal refines and sells common salt for edible and industrial applications. Products include free-flow iodized salt, industrial salt, double-fortified salt and half-dry salt. Refining, drying, quality testing and packing can earn more value than simply reselling raw or finished salt, but the enterprise remains a mixed manufacturer/trader. FY26 manufactured goods were ₹118.17 crore, about 59.2% of operating revenue; traded goods were ₹81.44 crore, about 40.8%. The prior-year split was ₹67.86/₹62.11 crore. The company sells through wholesalers, industrial buyers and government/public-distribution contracts, so retail-outlet claims are not equivalent to direct consumer ownership or recurring retail revenue.

Rajasthan operations are complemented by Gujarat's Moti Chirai/Gandhidham unit. The issuer reports an April 2025 launch and audited notes identify 4 May 2025 commercial production. Proximity to salt sources and ports can reduce raw-material and freight friction. Promoter-linked salt works provide some raw supply, creating both reliability and related-party pricing questions. Customers are granted credit and inventories must be carried through procurement/weather cycles; cash is made only when invoices collect, not when inventory or a government order grows. Historical top-ten customer concentration was 68.47% in FY23, not a verified FY26 share. Current customer/product/geographic profitability and mature-versus-new-unit economics are ND. Exim/Foods may extend exports and salt capacity, but no revenue or profit is inserted into FY26 before ownership existed. [S1][S4][S6][S9][S10]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The most plausible advantage is landed cost, consistent quality and established distribution relationships, not a protected technology. Salt is bulky relative to value; sourcing, freight, plant reliability and a qualified supplier relationship can matter. These mechanisms merit investigation but do not establish persistent excess returns. Customer concentration, substantial traded revenue, competitive tendering, weather exposure and the ease of rival capacity constrain pricing. The company's descriptions of being the largest refinery or reaching every household are management positioning, not independently verified market-share evidence.

Three relevant primary-source contrasts help avoid a false peer multiple. Tata Consumer's FY26 salt review reports 14% revenue growth and a 100 bp market-share gain, illustrating the strength of a national branded/distribution franchise; its diversified group valuation is not a salt-only multiple. Ankur Chemfood is a closer operating comparison: Infomerics reports FY26 provisional sales ₹295.14 crore, 3.16% EBITDA margin, 1.63× interest cover and 467, 000 MTPA across five plants. Its thin margins show how difficult durable excess economics can be, although differing mix and accounting prevent mechanically equating its margins with Goyal's. Vibrant Global Salt's June 2026 CRISIL B/Stable/A4 issuer-not-cooperating classification is an information-risk comparator, not a default finding or current earnings benchmark. Goyal's own June BBB−/Stable/A3 reaffirmation is materially better credit evidence than that weak comparator. MOAT4 reflects contestability while recognizing useful operations; it does not penalize the company solely for small size. [S1][S4][S6][P1–P3]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Comparable standalone operating revenue is ₹60.0530/66.1109/117.6418/117.7455/129.9720/199.6024 crore for FY21–FY26. The selected five-year CAGR is 27.15%, with six observations. FY23–FY26 three-year CAGR is 19.27%. FY20 revenue ₹71.4898 crore gives an 18.66% six-year context, showing why the depressed FY21 base should not be mistaken for a stable high-growth starting point. Ten-year CAGR is ND. Annual additions from FY22 onward are ₹6.0579, 51.5309, 0.1037, 12.2265 and 69.6304 crore. The near-flat FY24 matters alongside the strong FY26.

FY26's manufacturing addition ₹50.3026 crore was larger than its trading addition ₹19.3278 crore, consistent with a real capacity ramp. Manufacturing increased 74.12%; trading 31.12%. This is not an acquisition-led FY26 consolidated jump: audited results are standalone and the new subsidiaries enter later. Nevertheless, comparable tonnes, prices, product mix and contract mix after FY23 are not separately established, so reported nominal growth is not labeled constant-price organic volume growth. IPO volumes show total FY23 tonnage of 260, 105.57 versus 182, 482.43 in FY22 and 197, 402.83 in FY21, but those totals combine products and cannot become a new-unit utilization measure.

Latest comparable half-years are H1FY26 ₹88.1906 crore versus derived H1FY25 ₹68.2589 crore, growth 29.20%, and H2FY26 ₹111.4118 versus ₹61.7131 crore, growth 80.53%. H2 is the audited-year balancing figure, not an independently audited seasonal quarter. No verified H1FY27 financials were available by cutoff; TTM remains FY26. REV starts at 8 for 27.15% and receives exactly one −1 base-distortion adjustment to 7, supported by the longer/shorter windows. No further small-base penalty or forecast-growth bonus is applied. [S1–S5][S12]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The runway is primarily utilization of commissioned capacity, product/channel mix and Gujarat logistics, rather than an unbounded salt TAM. The issuer describes 450, 000 MTPA new capacity plus 210, 000 MTPA Rajasthan capacity, totaling 660, 000 MTPA. Earlier IPO tables showed 310, 000 MTPA and the new annual narrative also mentions 2600 MT/day including a Phalodi/group reference. These definitions do not reconcile automatically; promoter-group facilities are not listed-company property. We retain 660, 000 as an attributed operating constraint, not certified capacity available for every product.

The embedded bottom-up test assumes, rather than claims, 65% manufactured revenue and ₹4, 500 realization per tonne. It converts each scenario's annual sales into manufacturing tonnes and utilization, flags any requirement above 660, 000 tonnes, and shows a rough incremental-capacity capital proxy using management's ₹80 crore/450, 000 MT project claim. Changing realization or mix changes this constraint. The bull eventually requires more capacity than the attributed base, so its return depends on expansion and effective deployment, not just filling an idle plant. Maintenance capex is not separately disclosed; annual total capex is modeled explicitly and stressed higher. D&A is not called maintenance capex.

ONWC expanded from ₹26.15 crore to ₹48.06 crore as new operations required inventory and credit. The annual model funds every working-capital increment, operating deposit and capex amount, retains a 1% sales operating cash floor, and amortizes term debt. No ordinary scenario is promoted to a return when it breaches that floor. A17.44% one-year incremental book-ROIC proxy is informative but not attributable plant returns; CAP stays NS. GQS therefore remains NS, with the separate cap 5 from CASH3. The practical question is whether capacity can create cash per share without repeated adverse financing, not whether a facility exists. [S1][S3][S4][S6]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter ownership is 72.61% in the March 2026 disclosure and the same 17, 900, 250 issued shares remain in the October security master. The disclosure reports no promoter pledge, warrants or outstanding ESOPs at March; it is not proof of an unchanged October encumbrance position. Statutory and secretarial opinions in the annual report are unmodified. The May 11 CRISIL note said information was awaited and explicitly was not a reaffirmation; June 2 subsequently reaffirmed BBB−/Stable/A3. It would be misleading to retain only May's warning or to call June's opinion a current facility sanction.

Stewardship concerns are concrete but not established misconduct: quoted-equity investing alongside operating borrowings; historical cash-flow reclassification; commercial family-supplier transactions; and director tenure continuity. The September notice states that three executive appointments expired 21 May 2026, describes continued work at the board's request, and seeks ratification/new terms from 1 October. The voting-result reference was located, but detailed votes were not retrieved. Final ratification is not assumed, and no unsupported legal-invalidity conclusion is drawn. FY26 related purchases sum to about ₹5.623 crore, and the company represents transactions as ordinary-course/arm's-length. Remuneration ₹0.558 crore in employee expense differs from three ₹18.75 lakh lines totaling ₹0.5625 crore in the RPT note, plus sitting fees. The small ₹0.0045 crore discrepancy is flagged without exaggerating materiality.

Promises versus delivery: the Gujarat plant launch 20 April 2025 is followed by commercial production 4 May and ₹50.30 crore manufactured-revenue addition in FY26, a genuine delivered milestone. The claim of 5, 000 retail outlets and national household reach remains management ambition, with no channel-level economics verified. Capitalization of ₹1.0265 crore pre-operative expense and ₹0.6547 crore interest is disclosed, not assumed operating cash generation. October Foods rights subscriptions increase the holding to 30.60 lakh shares; the proposed ₹10 crore subsidiary-loan envelope is not proof of approval or disbursement. IPO-disclosed quality/misbranding cases were pending then; latest outcomes are ND, so no conviction or exoneration is invented. GOV5 and EXEC6 capture the mixed record without a governance override. [S1][S4][S6–S11]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The historical table and full cash ledgers are embedded. FY26 operating EBITDA is ₹24.2305 crore and EBIT ₹18.2758 crore after excluding other income, compared with FY25 EBITDA ₹11.9445 crore. Reported PAT fell from ₹13.2469 to ₹11.3526 crore because FY25 included ₹7.3058 crore investment gains. Removing all other income and applying an analyst 25% tax rate gives normalized PAT proxies of ₹4.2913, ₹7.4111 and ₹11.2793 crore for FY24–FY26. These are sensitivities, not restated audited profits. Published EPS of ₹6.34 versus ₹7.40 is retained; older weighted EPS is not silently compared with current-share economic EPS.

Cash requires reconciliation at two levels. Original FY24 CFO of ₹15.4614 crore became ₹5.0766 crore in the FY25 comparative, with a near-equal financing offset. FY23 prospectus CFO of ₹3.2993 crore differs from the later −₹2.0799 crore comparative. We use the later FY24 figure and limit cumulative conversion to FY24–FY26; alternatives remain visible. Investment gains of ₹6.2440 and ₹7.3058 crore stayed in reported operating cash in FY24/FY25. Removing gross gains and adding back FY26's investment loss as a classification sensitivity leaves ₹1.7154 crore cumulative CFO before financing interest, versus ₹15.2448 crore reported. After interest, the sensitivity is −₹2.8271 crore. Investment-sale receipts and related taxes are not independently reconciled, so this is not certified corrected CFO. Neither accounting ambiguity nor a clean audit opinion alone settles G2.

FY26's operating bridge reconciles: ₹24.3628 crore before working capital, less ₹22.6137 crore working-capital absorption and ₹3.8842 crore tax, equals CFO of −₹2.1351 crore. The printed cash-generated line is only the working-capital subtotal and must not be subtracted twice. Inventory of ₹28.6922 crore rose 107.54%, while receivables of ₹26.5687 crore rose 75.33%, both faster than revenue. Average receivable days improved with higher sales, an important counterpoint, while raw and packing stocks dominate inventory. Gross receivables older than one year of ₹1.3203 crore include ₹1.2254 crore older than three years. The ₹0.2316 crore provision is not a guarantee of recovery. Payables of ₹8.0638 crore supplied funding, mostly current rather than aged.

Debt is ₹44.3732 crore, including cash credit of ₹27.3372 crore and term debt of ₹17.0360 crore, without duplicating current maturities. Of ₹0.4857 crore reported cash, ₹0.2643 crore secures bank guarantees, leaving ₹0.2214 crore available. Quoted-equity cost of ₹5.6455 crore exceeds disclosed March market value of ₹2.5326 crore by ₹3.1129 crore. No current value or automatic impairment conclusion is invented. Bank guarantees of ₹2.571 crore and direct-tax contingency of ₹0.4201 crore are contingent, not automatically paid debt claims. Current net tax of ₹0.039 crore is distinct and paid once in the model. Operating invested capital of ₹105.0032 crore and prior ₹71.4420 crore reconciles to financing definitions. Normalized ROIC of 15.54%, EBIT interest cover of 5.65× and net debt/EBITDA of 1.82× are useful, but commissioning timing and missing current subsidiary statements prevent CAP or BAL conclusions. [S1–S6]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹100.75 and 17, 900, 250 shares, market capitalization is ₹180.3450 crore. Historical cross-checks are 15.89× FY26 reported earnings and 2.70× book. Adding March debt and subtracting only available cash and the stale March quoted-equity portfolio gives ₹221.9642 crore historical EV and 9.16× normalized EBITDA. This is not current October EV: cash, debt and subsequent subsidiary funding have not been rolled forward from verified accounts. No property value or IPO proceeds are added again. Operating rent stays in EBITDA, with no invented financing-lease claim.

The linked model contains a separate March-to-19 October conditional opening bridge, the remaining FY27 stub, FY28–FY31, and a 202/366-year FY32 stub ending 19 October 2031. It models sales, margins, depreciation, interest, cash tax, working capital, operating deposits, capex, term-debt repayment, shares and cash requirements. Base revenue growth is 18/15/13/12/10/8%, EBITDA margin 12%, ONWC 25.5% declining to 24% of sales, annual capex ₹8–11 crore, and terminal EV/EBITDA 9×. Bear margins fall to 8–9% with slower collections. Bull margins reach 15%, but its volume requirement eventually exceeds attributed existing capacity. All cases assume unverified continued cash-credit rollover; none receives an automatic overdraft when cash is negative.

The known ₹3.06 crore cumulative Foods equity subscription is deducted in the pre-entry bridge once. The proposed loan envelope of up to ₹10 crore is a separate funding sensitivity, not evidence of a draw. No unverified subsidiary profit, NCI value or residual investment recovery is added to parent value. The first rescue is explicitly hypothetical at the October entry, not an assertion that shares were actually issued before then.

All ordinary IRR and entry fields are null because current funding is unverified. All no-rescue conditional returns are also null because every path breaches the operating cash floor: peak gaps are ₹16.43 crore bear, ₹9.17 crore base and ₹4.14 crore bull. Separate base rescue at a 50% discount with 3% fees raises ₹9.4548 crore and adds 1, 876, 893 shares. Its 17.41% annualized return is not an ordinary base-case return. Corresponding bear and bull rescue returns are −13.95% and 39.77%. Discount sensitivities of 25/50/70%, fees of 0/3/6%, capex, working-capital, non-renewal, portfolio and contingency stresses are fully embedded. Execution costs of 0/1/3/5% each side and hurdle rates of 12/15/18% are separate tests.

The FCFF DCF begins after October entry. It deducts forecast operating reinvestment and growth in required cash. Terminal reinvestment equals next-period NOPAT times growth divided by terminal ROIC, with 3–5% growth, 12–16% terminal ROIC and 12–16% WACC. The operating cash floor is retained in terminal EV, not both distributed and retained; DCF includes both its entry funding requirement and future increases. At 14% WACC, 3% terminal growth and 12% terminal ROIC, the base operating DCF yields a financing-agnostic price around ₹53.69, with 68.31% of operating value from the terminal period. This is not an entry quote or funded fair value. The two-way growth/multiple grid preserves null returns for unfunded cells. A separate rescue reverse-grid first reaches the 15% hurdle near 10.8% constant growth under base economics and 9× exit, with explicitly dilutive financing. There is no ordinary entry range. [S3][S4][S9][S10][M1][M2]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear argument is not the disappearance of salt demand. It is that poor utilization, rising raw-material or freight costs, slow collections and seasonal inventory can occur together while working-capital lines are already heavily used. The Gujarat plant would then incur depreciation and fixed costs before producing enough cash. Funding a 51%-controlled subsidiary could absorb liquidity precisely when the parent needs it. Supplier credit, securities at book cost and a bank rating are not interchangeable with available cash.

The linked bear combines a first-year revenue decline of 10%, an 8% EBITDA margin and ONWC of 30–32% before partial recovery. It produces a peak unmet cash requirement of ₹16.43 crore even with cash-credit rollover. Explicit new-equity rescue still leaves a −13.95% annualized per-share return, roughly 53% five-year price impairment. The separate non-renewal stress calls the cash-credit balance instead of inventing fresh borrowing. Investment markdowns, aged customer balances, financing fees and dilution can make losses permanent; a quoted drawdown alone does not establish permanent impairment. Tax and bank-guarantee contingencies are optional additional claims, not amounts automatically counted as current debt.

Counterevidence is real: a commissioned plant, higher operating margins, June's stable rating and adequate-liquidity opinion, predominantly recent receivables, and no verified default. These facts keep G3 at Hold, not Fail. The thesis-break variable is sustainable cash after working capital and necessary capex relative to verified bank headroom and maturities. Impairment risk is High. Better collections and less capital-intensive growth could change the path, but cannot be inferred from a moderate historical P/E. [S4][S6][S9][S10]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold price outcome over five years requires 37.97% annual compounding; tenfold requires 58.49%. With unchanged shares, a 15× terminal P/E and 6% parent net margin, 5× requires approximately ₹1, 001.92 crore revenue and 10× approximately ₹2, 003.83 crore, versus ₹199.60 crore currently. These are algebraic requirements, not targets. New shares, a lower exit multiple, a smaller parent share of subsidiary profits and additional financing raise the operating burden.

The bottom-up capacity test already flags the bull's later manufacturing requirement above the attributed 660, 000 MTPA at an illustrative 65% manufactured mix and ₹4, 500 per tonne realization. No verified accessible-market share or financed project-return path supports a five-to-tenfold outcome. The company's ₹80 crore plant claim does not prove that new capacity can be added at the same marginal cost. Enterprise value can grow while per-share returns disappoint because financing absorbs the gain. Classification: Speculative / unsupported, not mathematically impossible. The next evidence needed is attributable cash returns and financed capacity, not a larger headline TAM. [S1][S4][M1][M2]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain the auditor-backed FY23/FY24 cash-flow bridges. The FY24 CFO difference is ₹10.3848 crore. Continued ambiguity keeps G2 on Hold; a coherent bank and statement reconciliation would improve confidence.
2. Track cash realization after appropriate operating/investing classification. Latest three-year reported CFO/PAT is 0.448×. Persistent weak operating cash despite the ramp is a warning; documented inability to pay obligations is a thesis break.
3. Refresh March cash-credit draw ₹27.3372 crore against the ₹30 crore limit, current cash, renewal dates and debt maturities. Sustained utilization above 95% matches the CRA's warning. Absent committed funds against required cash uses is decisive.
4. Require new-plant production, utilization, realization and attributable profit, with a reconciled capacity perimeter. Compare delivery with FY26 manufactured revenue ₹118.17 crore rather than promotional outlet counts.
5. Watch inventory ₹28.6922 crore, receivables ₹26.5687 crore and gross receivables over one year ₹1.3203 crore. Growth persistently faster than sales or increasing disputes requires investigation; demonstrated uncollectibility with capital erosion could break the thesis.
6. Reconcile treasury investments costing ₹5.6455 crore versus ₹2.5326 crore March market value, cash proceeds, taxes and impairment policy. Do not assume a subsequent recovery.
7. Track Foods' ₹3.06 crore equity investment, Exim funding and any draw/repayment of the ₹10 crore loan envelope through parent and consolidated accounts. A proposal or permission to lend is not evidence that cash moved.
8. Verify RPT pricing, the small remuneration-note difference, director-renewal compliance and latest product-case outcomes without presuming adverse findings.
9. On new results, monitor margins and EPS excluding investment gains, not just headline PAT.
10. Before any implementation, recheck the 600-share lot, complete 20/60-day observations, spread, queues and restrictions for the actual position. Median observed whole-lot capacity at 5% participation is zero; three October sessions dominate turnover. Review at new results and material filings. This is a research monitoring plan, not an automation or trading authorization. [S1–S10][M1][M2]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Goyal is a capacity-ramp, commodity-processing and trading thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder candidate. No aggregate point score is published: CAP and BAL are NS, Growth Quality remains NS despite its cash-quality cap, and IAS also lacks R and L. The material G2 reliability hold precludes an eligible investment classification and numerical quality ranking. Incomplete evidence is not ranked at the bottom as if it proved a poor business. G1 is not Fail and no severe-governance override is applied. Unverified current funding is not the same as a verified default.

Action category: Research priority / wait for evidence, not buy at a modeled rescue price. A new buyer would need reconciled cash accounts, current consolidated funding and attributable plant returns before price could drive a supported decision. An existing holder should review the thesis and actual position's execution constraints; holdings, cost basis, taxes and portfolio weights were not supplied, so no exit quantity or trade is invented. The positive base-rescue IRR cannot fill the R factor, and a cheaper quote cannot resolve historical cash ambiguity. Upside depends on manufacturing scale becoming dependable cash per share; the decisive risk is growth financed through borrowing, dilution and group cash uses without clear owner economics. [S1–S10][M1][M2]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Evidence comes from exchange-filed annual reports, the issuer's prospectus, results and shareholding copies, official NSE security and bhavcopy records, and primary rating/peer publications. IDs, dates, page locators, original URLs and SHA256 hashes accompany material claims. Management statements, credit opinions and analyst assumptions remain distinguished from verified outcomes. Both private archives exclude original issuer PDFs, raw HTML, OCR, page images and personal identifiers. They retain financial-only extracts, models, source references, code and QA results. Offline reproduction verifies internal consistency, not original-source authenticity; fresh authentication requires downloading the original URLs and comparing hashes.

Open questions are the auditor's historical cash-flow bridge; investment-sale proceeds and tax classification; impairment policy; current cash, bank renewal and headroom; Foods/Exim funding and consolidated NCI; any subsidiary-loan draw; new-plant economics and capacity perimeter; recent volume/price decomposition and customer concentration; remuneration-note reconciliation; product-case outcomes; and complete calendar liquidity with current queues. Forecast growth, margins, working capital, capex, tax, terminal multiples, cash floor, portfolio residual value and rescue pricing are assumptions, not management commitments. The 25% tax rate, 15% equity hurdle and 12–16% WACC are separate choices. No historical IPO cash or operating property is added again. No trade or external outreach was performed as part of this research. [S1–S13][P1–P3][M1][M2]

evidence.claim: Verified exact issuer: Goyal Salt Limited, NSE SME GOYALSALT, ISIN INE0QFE01017. Issued shares 17, 900, 250; lot 600; official 19 October 2026 close ₹100.75.
evidence.locator: Company details and exact-ISIN exchange records.

evidence.claim: FY21–FY26 standalone revenue is ₹60.0530, 66.1109, 117.6418, 117.7455, 129.9720, 199.6024 crore. Five-year CAGR 27.1529%; three-year 19.2710%; FY20 context ₹71.4898 crore.
evidence.locator: IPO summary pp 66–68 and latest statutory P&L; FY21 original comparative.
evidence.limitation: Revenue scope is comparable. FY21 is a depressed base; earnings and cash-flow reclassifications are separately retained.

evidence.claim: Manufactured revenue rose from ₹67.8630 to ₹118.1656 crore in FY26; traded revenue from ₹62.1090 to ₹81.4368 crore. Gujarat commercial production began 4 May 2025; launch on 20 April is a different milestone.
evidence.locator: Annual report Note 20 and commissioning Note 8, p 87.
evidence.limitation: Comparable FY26 volume and realization were not disclosed; growth is not all attributed to volume.

evidence.claim: Original FY24 CFO ₹15.4614 crore became ₹5.0766 crore in the FY25 comparative. The financing offset is ₹10.3847 crore against a ₹10.3848 crore CFO change. FY23 IPO CFO ₹3.2993 differs from later −₹2.0799 crore.
evidence.locator: S1 p 68; S2 p 65, visually checked; S3 p 78.
evidence.limitation: An explicit auditor bridge was not located. Later comparative used; an offset alone does not establish full reconciliation.

evidence.claim: FY24–FY26 reported CFO ₹15.2448 crore divided by PAT ₹34.0527 crore is 0.44768256×. Cash capex is ₹57.2464 crore and FCF −₹42.0016 crore. Gross investment-gain removal sensitivity leaves CFO ₹1.7154 crore before interest and −₹2.8271 crore after interest.
evidence.locator: Cash-flow statements, investment-income notes and model ledgers.
evidence.limitation: Transaction-level sale receipts and tax allocation were not reconciled; the adjustment is a sensitivity, not corrected audited CFO.

evidence.claim: FY26 pre-working-capital cash ₹24.3628 crore minus WC absorption ₹22.6137 crore minus tax ₹3.8842 crore equals CFO −₹2.1351 crore. The printed cash-generated line is only the WC subtotal.
evidence.locator: Annual report p 71 / PDF74, visually inspected.
evidence.limitation: Unmodified audit opinion preserved. A mislabeled subtotal does not create a second cash outflow.

evidence.claim: March FY26 debt ₹44.3732 crore; reported cash ₹0.4857 crore includes ₹0.2643 crore restricted BG deposits, leaving ₹0.2214 crore available. CC draw ₹27.3372 crore against ₹30 crore gives nominal March headroom ₹2.6628 crore, not verified October funding.
evidence.locator: Borrowing and cash Notes 4, 8, 18 and 4.1; June rating.
evidence.limitation: June BBB−/Stable/A3 reaffirmation is counterevidence. Average line utilization exceeded 85%, with some months above 95%; no default is asserted.

evidence.claim: FY26 receivables ₹26.5687 crore increased 75.33%; inventory ₹28.6922 crore increased 107.54%. Gross receivables over one year are ₹1.3203 crore and over three years ₹1.2254 crore; doubtful provision ₹0.2316 crore.
evidence.locator: Inventory, receivable and ageing notes 16, 17 and 17.1.
evidence.limitation: Supplier credit increased; most receivables remain undisputed and under six months old.

evidence.claim: Quoted investments cost ₹5.6455 crore versus disclosed March market value ₹2.5326 crore, a ₹3.1129 crore difference. FY24/FY25 investment gains ₹6.2440/₹7.3058 crore boosted profits and were not removed from reported CFO.
evidence.limitation: Other-than-temporary impairment judgment is unresolved; no accounting violation is asserted.

evidence.claim: Audits are unmodified; March promoter holding is 72.61% with no reported pledge, warrants or ESOP. Executive terms expired 21 May 2026; the notice explains continued service and seeks ratification/renewal from 1 October.
evidence.locator: Audit, AGM notice and shareholding declarations. Voting-result landing page is only a pointer; detailed votes unverified.
evidence.limitation: No fraud or disqualification is inferred; the board-requested continuity explanation is retained.

evidence.claim: FY26 related-party purchases total about ₹5.623 crore. Employee-remuneration note is ₹0.5580 crore versus ₹0.5625 crore for three directors in the RPT note, plus ₹0.006 crore sitting fees. Difference ₹0.0045 crore remains open.
evidence.locator: Employee Note 25 and RPT notes pp 89–90.
evidence.limitation: Company says transactions are ordinary-course and arm’s-length; no independent pricing benchmark or misuse finding.

evidence.claim: Foods holding reached 3, 060, 000 shares at ₹10 by 13 October, implying cumulative equity investment ₹3.06 crore. It is 51%-controlled. The AGM notice proposes up to ₹10 crore, 9%, three years; final approval and actual draw are not verified.
evidence.locator: October rights filings and AGM loan note p 121.
evidence.limitation: Duplicate October 13 exchange copies are not counted twice. Current Exim subscription amount, consolidated cash and NCI are ND.

evidence.claim: Operating IC ₹71.4420/₹105.0032 crore reconciles to financing IC. FY26 normalized ROIC is 15.54% and one-year incremental book proxy 17.44%, against analyst WACC range 12–16%. CAP remains NS.
evidence.locator: Detailed ONWC and operating-versus-financing IC model.
evidence.limitation: No attributable cohort return. Full new-plant investment timing and subsidiary economics are unresolved.

evidence.claim: FY23 top-ten customer concentration was 68.47%, top-five 54.83%. A government-procurement paragraph contains an inconsistent amount/percentage and is not used as verified current mix.
evidence.limitation: Current customer concentration is ND; old concentration is not represented as current.

evidence.claim: Issuer claims 660, 000 MTPA capacity and 5, 000 outlets. Earlier IPO310, 000 MTPA and later 2600 MT/day descriptions require perimeter reconciliation. The 450, 000 MT Gujarat plant is commissioned, but the largest-refinery claim is unverified.
evidence.locator: Prospectus capacity table; annual report pp 3, 12 and MD&A.
evidence.limitation: Group Phalodi capacity is not automatically listed-company property;660, 000 MTPA remains an attributed claim.

evidence.claim: Official archives provide 49 issuer observations in 60 sessions, 15 in 20. Eight 600-share lots cost ₹483, 600; nine cost ₹544, 050. Observed-only 60-session median traded value is ₹413, 730, implying 23.38 theoretical days for the floor position at 5% participation.
evidence.locator: Issuer-specific daily archive extracts and lot analysis.
evidence.limitation: L remains NS. Missing issuer rows are not zero; spreads and queues are unknown. The 14–16 October burst dominates recent turnover.

evidence.claim: All no-rescue scenarios breach required operating cash; ordinary and no-rescue conditional returns stay null. Base peak gap ₹9.1712 crore; separate rescue gross ₹9.4548 crore at 50% discount and 3% fees adds 1, 876, 893 shares.
evidence.locator: Annual conditional funding model and separately labeled rescue models.
evidence.limitation: The October opening bridge is conditional, not actual. Rollover is unverified; rescue does not establish an ordinary return.

evidence.claim: Peer contrast: Tata Salt 14% FY26 revenue growth and brand share gain; Ankur FY26 provisional 3.16% EBITDA margin and 1.63× interest cover; Vibrant June 2026 B/Stable/A4 issuer-not-cooperating status.
evidence.locator: Named primary company and rating documents.
evidence.limitation: Different business perimeters and provisional/rating information preclude mechanical valuation comparisons.

evidence.claim: The IPO disclosed two product-quality/misbranding proceedings then pending. Later final outcomes were not verified.
evidence.limitation: Pending proceedings are not convictions or present findings of a violation; no fabricated clearance.
